subject.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback

question: Should a configured `gateway.auth.token` SecretRef shadowed by `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` be treated as a warning that fails Doctor lint, even though current documentation defines the environment token as the winning active surface?
rationale: The code can implement any of the choices safely, but warning severity, remediation wording, and whether existing lint automation should start failing are security-policy and compatibility decisions rather than mechanically decidable defects.

options.title: Separate precedence from failure
options.body: Warn only when an active SecretRef resolution actually fails into fallback, while treating documented environment precedence as informational or non-finding behavior.

options.title: Adopt strict warnings
options.body: Keep the current audit and Doctor warnings for every configured SecretRef shadowed by environment credentials, and document the resulting lint compatibility change.

options.title: Audit only for now
options.body: Land plugin-path and SecretRef audit visibility but omit the Doctor lint contribution until the long-term credential-precedence policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Separate precedence from failure
recommendation.body: Warn only when an active SecretRef resolution actually fails into fallback, while treating documented environment precedence as informational or non-finding behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly extends the SecretRef active-surface and resolution contracts introduced in their merged feature work.
